name: BOMA International homepage: the commercial real estate trade association's landing page
title: BOMA International homepage: the commercial real estate trade association's landing page
answer: This is the homepage of BOMA International, the commercial real estate trade association, and its education arm BOMI. It is a promotional landing page rather than a report, and it does not mention artificial intelligence, smart buildings, energy efficiency or predictive maintenance anywhere in the harvested text. Its most useful content is a clear statement of scope: BOMA and BOMI serve property owners, managers and service providers across office, industrial, retail, hospitality, healthcare, government and educational buildings, offering advocacy, credentials and education. Readers should treat it as background on the organisation, not as evidence about AI.

sections.body: BOMA International publishes this page, the homepage of its website, alongside its education institute BOMI. It is a marketing and membership landing page for a commercial real estate trade association and credential provider, not a research report, article or dataset. Its scope is organisational: it describes who BOMA and BOMI serve, which building types they cover, and what they offer members, namely advocacy, legislative influence, education, credentials, business tools, programs and workforce development. The text states no publication date and no author. It notes that BOMI reunited with BOMA International after 50 years and describes itself as the number one commercial real estate educational provider in North America.
sections.heading: What this source is

sections.body: The page presents BOMA International and BOMI as the leading trade association and credential provider in commercial real estate, and as partners professionals choose to maximise value for their careers, organisations and assets. BOMI is described as dedicated to improving the skills of people with property, facilities and building operations responsibilities across every asset class: office, industrial, retail, hospitality, healthcare, government and educational buildings. BOMA and BOMI say they support property owners, managers, professionals and service providers of all commercial building types through advocacy, influence and education, and that they facilitate connections and provide resources, legislative advocacy and professional credential opportunities. The page positions the organisation as a future-focused advocate, connecting members with resources, partners and expertise, and says it stays on the leading edge of trends, policies and workforce development. It lists committee participation, advocacy involvement, business tools, programs and workforce development initiatives as the tools it provides. A membership section promotes negotiated discounts and rebates on building supplies, office supplies, express shipping and merchant services. The closing lines argue that joining a trade association is an investment in the community you serve, and that efficiency comes from surrounding yourself with experts. The tone throughout is promotional, aimed at recruiting members and credential candidates rather than reporting findings.
sections.heading: What it says

sections.body: The text gives few hard figures. It states that BOMI reunited with BOMA International after 50 years, and that BOMI is the number one commercial real estate educational provider in North America, a claim the page makes about itself without evidence. It lists seven asset classes served: office, industrial, retail, hospitality, healthcare, government and educational buildings. It names no statistics on buildings, energy use, maintenance costs or technology adoption, and gives no definition of artificial intelligence or smart buildings.
sections.heading: Figures and claims worth noting

sections.body: A reader following AI in real estate would find this page useful only as background on the organisation behind the claim, not as evidence for it. The harvested text contains no mention of artificial intelligence, smart-building operations, energy efficiency or predictive maintenance, so it cannot support a statement that BOMA tracks AI in those areas. What it does establish is BOMA's remit: a trade association and credential body covering commercial building operations across office, industrial, retail, hospitality, healthcare, government and education, with advocacy and education as its main levers. That scope explains why the organisation is relevant to AI adoption in commercial property, but the specifics would have to come from other BOMA material, such as its research, standards or education programmes.
sections.heading: What it means for AI in Real Estate

sections.body: This is a commercial landing page with almost no substantive content. It is promotional, written to attract members and credential candidates, and it carries no date, author or methodology. It does not cover artificial intelligence, smart buildings, energy efficiency or predictive maintenance, so it does not support the claim it was cited for. It offers no data, no case studies and no technical detail, and its one comparative claim, that BOMI is the number one educational provider in North America, is self-reported. Anyone needing evidence on AI in commercial real estate should look to BOMA's research publications, reports or course materials rather than this homepage.
